answer.evidence: The column scan is empty and the width profile reads 0 for every row, so I judged from the magnified image. It shows a roughly circular, checkerboard-dithered glow across rows 0-15, brightest at the centre and fading toward the edges. It has no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no vertical face and no ellipse rim. It is a flat floor decal seen from directly above, with no front face. That is the expected look for a flat object.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small round glow blob on a dark background, not a 4x3-tile ground patch like the grass and paving references. It has no grain, speckle, tufts or per-element shading, so it lacks the texture of the grass reference (26 colours per tile, 80 colours in total). It is also far sparser than the paving reference, whose stones are shaded one by one. There is no outline, so that check cannot help it. It would look thinner and flatter than either reference, and the piece is too small and ambiguous to show Beodeul-level craft, so it fails.
